thread:
Maya: Quick idea 1: express hosting/dedicated/private routing as a tiny declarative policy instead of ad-hoc flags.
Jonah: Yes. Makes precedence and rollouts auditable.
Priya: Sketch: route_policy { prefer:[private,dedicated,hosted], constraints:{data_residency:"local-only", max_latency_ms:120}, fallbacks:["shared-cache"] }
Sree: Add runtime knobs: max_probe_rate_per_min and sticky_fallback_minutes to avoid probe storms.
Devon: Important: model-pin and kms constraints must trump policy. Policy can only relax, not override pinning.
Maya: Telemetry: each request should record policy_id, decision_reason, and decision_path for tracing.
Jonah: Also add a dry_run mode on policy (pct,duration) so we can preview routing without enforcement.
Priya: UX: Console should simulate policy against recent traffic to show where traffic would route.
Devon: Tests: unit precedence table, integration harness that simulates tail latencies and validates probe limits.
ops-bot: RFC draft opened: https://go/repo/pulls/4102 title: "Policy-driven routing for hosting abstractions (draft)"
Maya: I'll author RFC and include migration plan for existing flags.
Jonah: Keep DSL small for now, iterate after one sprint. :thumbsup:
